content:
Hi all,

Excited to share a family of experimental libraries exploring Lean 4 as a systems programming language (https://github.com/pb64-lean):

  • rules_lean: Bazel rules for Lean 4 and Lake with an emphasis on cross-language native builds
  • grpc-lean: protobuf[1] code generation and a gRPC client/server runtime over HTTP/2
  • tls13-lean: TLS 1.3 code using HACL* as a trusted component for the crypto primitives
  • pg-lean: a PostgreSQL 17/18 client with TLS 1.3, SCRAM, md5, etc.
  • protovalidate-lean: An implementation of protovalidate support that translates CEL expressions annotating proto messages into Lean subtypes of the base generated message types
  • lean-acme-widgets: example service that uses all the pieces together

[1] Huge acknowledgement owed to https://github.com/Lean-zh/protobuf which was extended to round out proto3 support and the gRPC service codegen. It's kept under third_party/ with the hope to upstream any useful generic pieces

This is all experimental as-is - only the correctness of the generated validation code in protovalidate-lean has associated proofs. I have been approaching it from functionality first but hoping to attach more proofs, especially for the HTTP/2 protocol and the TLS 1.3 state machine.

The part I'm most excited about is protovalidate-lean:

  • it allows I/O validation close to the network boundary and yields types with propositions usable in Lean while still attached to protobuf message structures
  • because the standard pattern is that the relations are validated as a runtime check (e.g. in Java: https://github.com/bufbuild/protovalidate-java#protovalidate-java), the generated Lean code includes a runtime check corresponding to the refinement, rather than trusting inputs
  • this fits nicely into what is needed for authorization code to constrain access for an RPC - typically it can be expressed as a CEL expression on a message that includes the authenticated Principal etc. such as in an RBAC model
  • an example of RPC authorization implemented using this idea is in lean-acme-widgets
  • a future motivating concept: translating the relational constraints in a Postgres DB into Lean propositions at build time and generate a comparable runtime check into refined subtypes of objects returned from a DB query. (sqlx and jOOQ are my personal reference points for sql codegen tools that do really well in this kind of build model)

Looking forward to any discussion!
